You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"A voltage sag occurred on the utility power line, and the site has chillers that failed to restart, indicating mechanical cooling may have shut down. The rule's 'when' conditions include utility voltage sags and a portion of the datacenter transferring to generator power; while generator transfer is not explicitly stated, the voltage sag and cooling impact align with the rule's intent.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]},{"rule_id":"R-003","because":"Multiple chillers (13) failed to restart automatically and require manual intervention, and more than one data hall is affected (two adjacent data halls).","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S19"]},{"rule_id":"R-004","because":"Chillers have tripped offline and are being manually restarted; the chilled-water loop may be heating up because cooling is not yet restored. The rule applies during manual restart processes.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S80","AZ-AUE-2023:S81","AZ-AUE-2023:S82"]},{"rule_id":"R-005","because":"Chillers have tripped offline and are being manually restarted, and multiple data halls are affected. The rule requires verifying minimum chiller count per data hall.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S19","AZ-AUE-2023:S20"]},{"rule_id":"R-006","because":"Conditions that can cause utility voltage fluctuations (voltage sag occurred) are active, and the site relies on manual restart procedures for chillers (13 failed to restart automatically).","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them; if mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion; transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active.","rule_id":"R-001"},{"action":"Restart chillers in a data hall 'load based' sequence rather than an 'adjacent' sequence; ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling before completing restarts in any one hall; slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored.","rule_id":"R-003"},{"action":"Monitor the chilled-water loop temperature continuously during the restart process; if the loop temperature reaches a level that inhibits chiller restart, stop attempting restarts and take action to cool the loop; consider shutting down IT load to allow the chilled-water loop to return to a safe temperature so chillers can be restarted.","rule_id":"R-004"},{"action":"Confirm how many chillers each data hall requires to be operational; prioritize restarts to bring each data hall to at least its minimum required chiller count as quickly as possible; if a data hall cannot reach its minimum, escalate and consider load shedding.","rule_id":"R-005"},{"action":"Increase technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of chillers; ensure enough technicians are available to perform restarts in a load-based sequence across all impacted data halls.","rule_id":"R-006"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","reason":"Mechanical cooling confirmed shut down (13 chillers failed to restart) while storms remain active in the area, as per R-001 escalation trigger."},"not_covered":[]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"The voltage sag caused cooling system chillers for multiple datacenters to shut down."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Incremental load increases over time in the Availability Zone resulted in a chiller operating configuration that was susceptible to a timing defect in the Chiller Management System."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"By the time the team reached the final five chillers requiring a manual restart, the water inside the pump system for these chillers (chilled water loop) had reached temperatures that were too high to allow them to be restarted."},{"id":"F4","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"In this scenario, the restart is inhibited by a self-protection mechanism that acts to prevent damage to the chiller that would occur by processing water at the elevated temperatures."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"At 11:34 UTC, as temperatures continued to increase, our onsite datacenter team began a remote shutdown of remaining networking, compute, and storage infrastructure in the impacted data halls to protect data durability, infrastructure health, and address the thermal runaway."},{"id":"F6","kind":"response","text":"This shutdown allowed the chilled water loop to return to a safe temperature which allowed us to restart the chillers."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We have de-risked this failure to restart due to voltage fluctuations, by implementing a change to the control timing logic on the Chiller Management System (Completed)."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"Emergency Operation Procedure for manual restarts of simultaneous chiller failures has changed from an ‘adjacent’ sequence to a data hall ‘load based’ sequence to ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling, to slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored (Completed)."},{"id":"F9","kind":"remediation","text":"Following this incident, as a temporary mitigation, we increased technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of our chillers prior to the change to the Chiller Management System to prevent restart failures."},{"id":"F10","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Based on our incident analysis the staffing levels at the time would have been sufficient to prevent impact if a ‘load based' chiller restart sequence had been followed, which we have since implemented (Completed)."},{"id":"F11","kind":"impact","text":"At 10:30 UTC some networking, compute, and storage infrastructure began to shutdown automatically as data hall temperatures increased, impacting service availability."}]}
